items.description: A job requisition is a vacancy that an employer wants to fill

clientRequisitionID.description: The client assigned / managed requisition ID

requisitionDescription.description: A job requisition description to be used when published.  May differ based on the channel and whether published internally or externally

job.description: A reference to the related job entity

position.description: A reference to the related position entity

positionID.description: The unique identifier of the associated position

positionCode.description: A code of the to the related postion entity

categoryCode.description: A category code of the to the related postion entity

careerLevelCode.description: A code classifying the desired level of a potential worker based on career experience. Student, Entry Level, Recent Graduate, Mid-Career, Manager, Experienced Non-Manager, Senior Executive, etc.

requisitionLocations.description: A list of possible work locations as related to a given requisition

items.description: The work location of the associated position

nameCode.description: The location type code and description, e.g. HDQ, headquarters

address.description: An address related to the associated entity

aliasNames.description: The list of other names, by which a location is known

items.description: The code for the related entity.  If this is a coded value, codeValue and shortName should be used. If this is just a string value, only shortName is necessary

typeCode.description: The code for the related entity, e.g. division, region, district

nameValue.description: The name for the related location

hiringIndicator.description: Indicates if there are still any openings in the given Location against the Requisition.

primaryIndicator.description: Designates the location being primary based on the business requirements

postingIndicator.description: Designates the if the current location is a posting location

activeIndicator.description: Designates if location is enabled or not

locationIndependentIndicator.description: An indicator to identify a requisitions that should be returned to the job seeker all of the time, regardless of the location selected by the job seeker.  Another example could be a National Sales Manager that is based out of Los Angeles but the job seeker could live in NY

hiringManager.description: A hiring manager for a given position

recruiter.description: A recruiter associated with a given position

requisitionReasonCode.description: A code classifying the reason for the related requisition, e.g. new position or replacement

requisitionPurposeCode.description: A code classifying the purpose for the related requisition, e.g. normal, sourcing, system, etc.

internalIndicator.description: Indicates whether the requistion is posted to an internal job board and should be visible only to internal applicants. Can be used in conjunction with the externalIndicator

externalIndicator.description: Indicates whether the requistion is posted to an external job board and should be visible only to external applicants.  Can be used in conjunction with the internalIndicator

evergreenIndicator.description: An evergreen job is also known as recurring job to fill a position which is always open in a company - because it needs number of people for that position and doesn't have a particular target date to fill the position

priorityIndicator.description: This is an internal tracking indicator for the recruiters to indicate if a job should be filled by priority or not. This helps them to understand the priority of the jobs and take necessary actions to recruit people for the priority jobs

salaryVisibleIndicator.description: This is an indicator for the recruiters to indicate if the salary information should be displayed to the candidate.

locationVisibleIndicator.description: This is an indicator for the recruiters to indicate if the location information should be displayed to the candidate.

postDate.description: A date the requsition was published.  Could be used to determine the requisition age

positionQualifications.description: Qualifications required for a given position referenced by the related job requisition.  Typically to include summary, competencies, educations requirements, experience, licenses, etc.

qualificationSummary.description: Summary of qualifications - a container of information related to matching knowledge, skills, abilities, and other resource deployment-related characteristics (including competencies) offered by a candidate and/or demanded by a potential employer or customer

positionTravelRequirement.description: Denotes the percentage or other expression of expected travel for the position

nameCode.description: The requirement code and name

organizationalUnits.description: A list of organizational units the given job requistion is related to / owned by

nameCode.description: A coded name or descriptive label of the associated organizational unit entity. If this is a coded value, codeValue and shortName should be used. If this is just a string value, only shortName is necessary

alternateIDs.description: Collection of alternate IDs to reference the org unit

typeCode.description: The organizational unit code and description, e.g. department code.

allocationPercentage.description: The percentage a worker is allocated to the related organizational unit

effectiveDateTime.description: Effective date/time for the the organizational unit code information

standardHours.description: The standard number of hours of work associated to a position, typically used to drive the definition of a full time assignment, e.g. 40 in the US, 37.5 in the UK, 35 in FR. This number is usually expressed based on a week

payScaleCode.description: The pay scale for the related job requisition, e.g. salary admin plan

payGradeCode.description: The pay / salary grade for the related job requisition

payGradeRange.description: The pay / salary grade for the related job requisition

bonusEligibleIndicator.description: Indicates whether the position is bonus eligible

remunerationBasisCode.description: The remuneration basis code is a way of classifying a work assignment as salaried, salaried plus commission, commission only, hourly or daily

workLevelCode.description: The work level code, e.g. Fulltime, Parttime

workArrangementCode.description: A work arrangement describes the time and place that work gets done on a regular basis. For example, a work assignment can be fully office based, fully field based, fully home based, or some combination thereof

assignmentTermCode.description: This describes whether a work assignment has a known end date. If the assignment does not have a scheduled or known end date, it is considerd a regular or permanent assignment. If an assignment has a known or scheduled end date, it is considered a temporary or fixed term assignment

workerTypeCode.description: An enumerated code value to describe the offering type as related to a given job requisition, (e.g. Direct Hire, Temp, Contract, Temp to Hire, Seasonal, etc.)

allowedOvertimeIndicator.description: Indicates whether the overtime is allowed.  Often relevant to a contractor offering type

allowedOvertimeQuantity.description: Allowed overtime.  Often relevant to a contractor offering type

mandatoryOvertimeIndicator.description: Indicates whether the overtime is mandatory

paidRelocationCode.description: A code to describe the paid relocation level as related to a given postion, (e.g. offered, partially, etc.)

projectedStartDate.description: A target start date for the worker hired for the related requsition

projectedEndDate.description: A projected end date for the worker hired for the related requsition if otehr than full-time

workingLanguageCode.description: The primary language of the position referenced by a given job requistion

openingsQuantity.description: The total number of openings for the associated job requisition

openingsNewPositionQuantity.description: The total number of openings that are for new postions as opposed to backfills

backfillWorkerPositions.description: List of the workers / positions being backfilled using the current requisition

openingsFilledQuantity.description: The number of openings already filled for the associated job requisition. Should not exceed the total number of openings

shiftWorkIndicator.description: Indicates if the position requires (or has a possibility) working in shifts

sponsorVisaIndicator.description: Indicates if the company will sponsor work visa

sponsoredVisaTypeCodes.description: List of the visa type the company will sponsor for a given requisition

laborUnionIndicator.description: Indicates if the job for the related requisition is a union job

laborUnionCode.description: Indicates the labor union code for the related requisition

bargainingUnitCode.description: A bargaining unit is a group of employees who are so grouped for the purpose of collective bargaining. A bargaining unit is also known as a local labor union

visibleToJobSeekerIndicator.description: Indicates if the requision is posted and should be available to job seekers.  The hiring manager / practitioner can reset this flag, so the requisition would not be returned to a job seeker, without deleting the actual requistion

visibleToExternalJobSeekerIndicator.description: Indicates if the requision should be available to job seekers, including external, e.g. unauthenticated users

itemID.description: The unique identifier of the requisition

companyName.description: Name of the company with the job requirement

applicationStatusCode.description: Provides application status to applicant.  e.g.  Applied, Rejected, Accepted etc.

applicationID.description: The unique identifier of the application, if available

appliedDate.description: The date when a jobseeker applied for a given requisition, if available

externalScreening.description: Screening and background verification for the job applicant by the external agency

screeningPackageID.description: The unique screening package ID, as there can be multiple screening/assessment packages managed by vendor

screeningTypeCode.description: Code identifying the screening type, e.g. background screening, assessment, etc.

agencyCode.description: Agency completing the screening and background verification status for the job applicant

applicationStatusCode.description: Application status, when the screening should be initiated

workedInCountry.description: Prior work location of the candidate

postingInstructions.description: The posting instructions for the related requisition

items.description: The work location of the associated position

nameCode.description: The name code of the corresponding posting instruction

postingChannel.description: The channel, the requisition is posted to, e.g. job board

jobRequisitionOverrides.description: Allows for alternate requisition properties for different posting channels

requisitionDescription.description: A job requisition description to be used when published.  May differ based on the channel and whether published internally or externally

requisitionPurposeCode.description: A code classifying the purpose for the related requisition, e.g. normal, sourcing, system, etc.

nameCode.description: The requirement code and name

internalIndicator.description: Indicates whether the requistion is posted to an internal job board and should be visible only to internal applicants. Can be used in conjunction with the externalIndicator

externalIndicator.description: Indicates whether the requistion is posted to an external job board and should be visible only to external applicants.  Can be used in conjunction with the internalIndicator

prospectReferralIndicator.description: Indicates whether the worker prospect can be referred for a given requistion.  The default value should be as per workerProspect.refer in user profile, while this indicator will override the default if supplied. If the value is omitted, the default should be respected

prospectReferralDateRange.description: The date range when the referrals are being accepted

resumeRequiredIndicator.description: Indicates whether the requistion requires the resume to apply

validityAttestationIndicator.description: Indicates whether the applicant needs to sign for truthfulness and completeness of the information provided

compensationVisibleIndicator.description: Indicates whether the salary information is visible to an applicant / job seeker

applicantLimit.description: The maximum number of applications accepted for a requisition posted accoring to the current instruction.

applicationAcceptedDateRange.description: The date range the applications should be accepted, e.g. in the case where it is already a pre-defined candidate, but regulations require the job to be posted

postDate.description: A date the requsition was published to a given channel

expireDate.description: A date the requsition is expiring from a given channel

applicationMethods.description: The list of methods that could be used to apply

typeCode.description: The type of the method, e.g. in-person, email, on-line, mail, etc.

contact.description: The contact person to apply to

instructions.description: The list of application instructions, e.g. driving directions, business hours, dress code, etc.

address.description: The address for in-person / mail applications

links.description: Related links, e.g. map link to the address

itemID.description: The unique identifier of the application method within a collection

lieDetectorAcknowledgementIndicator.description: Indicates whether the client mandates applicants to lie detector acknowledgement

actions.description: List of actions allowed against a related job requsition item

actionTitle.description: Human readable title of the action

actionTypeCode.description: Identifies the type of action to be taken to fulfill the request.  Action can be a callback to a service to complete the action.  A callback requires the methodCode and uris to be returned.  An external link i.e. open a web page - requires the uris of the external link; An object reference is a reference to a related object within the application.  This is a canonical name which represents the object.  Based on this identifier, the application knows what view it needs to open.  The uris returns the data for the view.  For an object reference, the objectRefID, methodCode, and uris are required . modify indicates that a property is being modified

defaultIndicator.description: True indicates that this is the default action

sequence.description: Sequence indicates that the item in the array must be in a sequence in relation to the other items in the sequence.  The action must not ocurr before another action with a lower sequence

meta.description: Meta contains the metadata associated with a response.  A GET response may include metadata to support pagination

linkType_v02.description: A link description object is used to describe link relations.  In the context of a schema, it defines the link relations of the instances of the schema, and can be parameterized by the instance values.  The link description format can be used on its own in regular (non-schema documents), and use of this format can be declared by referencing the normative link description schema as the the schema for the data structure that uses the links

linkID.description: Simple (string) identifier of an object to be used when there is no appropriate specific named ID Type

rel.description: Indicates the nature of the relationship of the related resource to the resource that generated this representation

canonicalUri.description: A unique identifier of the feature/function/operation, the link poins to

title.description: This property defines a title for the link.  The value must be a string. User agents MAY use this title when presenting the link to the user

targetSchema.description: This property is a schema that defines the expected structure of the JSON representation of the target of the link, if the target of the link is returned using JSON representation

mediaType.description: The media type that the linked resource will return (Response)

method.description: The HTTP method code (HTTP Verb) traverse the link (GET, POST, PUT or DELETE)

The query can be suffixed to the target URI to query the collection with property-based constraints on the resources that SHOULD be returned from the server or used to post data to the resource (depending on the method). nameCode.description: A coded name or descriptive label of the associated entity. If this is a coded value, codeValue and shortName should be used. If this is just a string value, only shortName is necessary

countryDialing.description: The country dialing code is the national prefix to be used when dialing TO that particular country FROM another country.

areaDialing.description: The local area dialing code for a telephone number.

dialNumber.description: The local communication number, not including country dialing or area dialing codes.   If component parts of the telephone number are being communicated then the dialNumber is required.

extension.description: The extension of the local communication number.  In the case of a Telephone Number accessing a Pager Network, the extension may be the Pager Identification Number required to leave a message for the Pager Number (i.e. Pager Pin).  These are mutually exclusive.

access.description: National Direct Dialing Prefix.  Also known as the trunk prefix or National Prefix.  It is the number to be dialed in a domestic telephone call, preceding any necessary area code and subscriber number (i.e. dial number).  When calling from outside of the country, the national direct dial prefix is omitted by the caller.  In Australia, Germany, and United Kingdom the trunk prefix is 0.  In the US and Canada it is 1.

formattedNumber.description: The formatted telephone number.  The component parts of the telephone are put together into a presentation pattern as defined by the regex format specified.  Please note that \ is used as an escape character in regex, but a double \ is needed to escape within the json schema.  The regex will accept +CC NNNNNNNNNNNNNN where + is the symbol indicating the caller to enter their country specific code to call from outside the country.  CC is the country code for an international number (optional), and the area code and dial number.  The local access code (i.e. 1 (201) 333 4444. 1 is the access code in US) is not passed.  The UI will present the phone number following its own presentation convention

The meta component associated to an event that allows for the adding or changing of an address, should use the links array associated to the indicator to define the list of addresses from which the user can select to set the address in context to be the same as.

durationType_v01.description: Represents the duration of time as represented by ISO 8601. Where the value space is a six dimensional space where the coordinates designate the Gregorian year, month, day, hour, minute, and second. The number of seconds can include decimal digits to arbitary pecision. PnYn MnDTnH nMnS, where: [n] is replaced by the value for each of the date and time elements that follow the [n]. Leading zeros are not required, but the maximum number of digits for each element should be agreed to by the communicating parties. The capital letters 'P', 'Y', 'M', 'W', 'D', 'T', 'H', 'M', and 'S' are designators for each of the date and time elements and are not replaced. P is the duration designator (historically called 'period') placed at the start of the duration representation. Y is the year designator that follows the value for the number of years. M is the month designator that follows the value for the number of months. D is the day designator that follows the value for the number of days. T is the time designator that precedes the time components of the representation. H is the hour designator that follows the value for the number of hours. M is the minute designator that follows the value for the number of minutes. S is the second designator that follows the value for the number of seconds. The number of seconds can include decimal digits to arbitrary precision

countryDialing.description: The country dialing code is the national prefix to be used when dialing TO that particular country FROM another country.

areaDialing.description: The local area dialing code for a telephone number.

dialNumber.description: The local communication number, not including country dialing or area dialing codes.   If component parts of the telephone number are being communicated then the dialNumber is required.

extension.description: The extension of the local communication number.  In the case of a Telephone Number accessing a Pager Network, the extension may be the Pager Identification Number required to leave a message for the Pager Number (i.e. Pager Pin).  These are mutually exclusive.

access.description: National Direct Dialing Prefix.  Also known as the trunk prefix or National Prefix.  It is the number to be dialed in a domestic telephone call, preceding any necessary area code and subscriber number (i.e. dial number).  When calling from outside of the country, the national direct dial prefix is omitted by the caller.  In Australia, Germany, and United Kingdom the trunk prefix is 0.  In the US and Canada it is 1.

formattedNumber.description: The formatted telephone number.  The component parts of the telephone are put together into a presentation pattern as defined by the regex format specified.  Please note that \ is used as an escape character in regex, but a double \ is needed to escape within the json schema.  The regex will accept +CC NNNNNNNNNNNNNN where + is the symbol indicating the caller to enter their country specific code to call from outside the country.  CC is the country code for an international number (optional), and the area code and dial number.  The local access code (i.e. 1 (201) 333 4444. 1 is the access code in US) is not passed.  The UI will present the phone number following its own presentation convention

amountValue.description: The numeric value associated to the rate. In the example 5 US dollars per hour, the number 5 is the rate value. In the example 3 bags of rice per month, the number 3 is the rate value. In the example, 20 percent of annual sales, the amountValue would be 20

currencyCode.description: List of standard currency codes ISO 4217 For any given rate, either the currencyCode or the unitCode is present. In the example 5 US dollars per hour, the unitCode would not be present, and the currency code would be USD

unitCode.description: For any given rate, either the currencyCode or the unitCode is present. In the example 3 bags of rice per month, currencyCode would not be present, and the unitCode would be bags of rice. In the example, 20 percent of annual sales, the unitCode would be percent

baseUnitCode.description: For any given rate, the baseUnitCode is used to define the denominator of the rate, or rate over what. In the example 5 US dollars per hour, the baseUnitCode is hour. In the example 3 bags of rice per month, the baseUnitCode is month. If for example, the rate was 10 US dollars for every widget produced, the baseUnitCode would be widget. In the example, 20 percent of annual sales, the baseUnitCode would equate to annual sales

baseMultiplierValue.description: For any given rate, the base rate value is presumed to be 1, e.g. per one hour, per one month. If for example, the rate was 10 US dollars for every widget produced, the base rate value is presumed to be one and there is no need to communicate a baseMultiplierValue. If however, the rate was 10 US Dollars for every 3 widgets produced, the baseMultiplierValue would be 3
